objective: Deliver a functional Rust + GTK4/libadwaita Linux port of FluentFlyout (media, lock-key and volume flyouts) on Fedora/GNOME Wayland, including reverse-engineering, implementation, validation and documentation.
operational_context: Autonomous delegation. All implementation slices, gates and documentation are complete; the remaining work is the final gate rerun and the delivery report.
ai_scope: Derive the behavioural specification and architectural decisions
Implement, test and document the Linux application
Run build, lint, test and runtime validation
human_scope: Approving visual deviations from the Windows original
Deciding whether the optional layer-shell build becomes the default
Validating on a real GNOME Shell session and on real lock-key hardware
Any decision to distribute binaries under GPL-3.0-or-later
open_questions: Should anchored flyouts use wlr-layer-shell by default on wlroots/KDE?
Is compositor-placed positioning acceptable on GNOME, or is a Shell extension required?
Should the interface be localised beyond English?
blockers: Next-Up flyout: MPRIS exposes no queue look-ahead
Taskbar widget/visualizer: requires Windows taskbar embedding; needs a separate GNOME Shell extension
Acrylic backdrop blur: no Wayland protocol for client-side backdrop blur
Global media-key hook: not available to Wayland clients

validation.renderer: Vulkan verified via GSK_RENDERER, /proc/self/maps and vulkaninfo (dzn / D3D12, RX 7600)
validation.not_executed: GNOME Shell placement, lock keys on real hardware, volume with a real sink, remote artwork, autostart

summary: FluentFlyout's media, lock-key and volume flyouts are reimplemented natively in Rust with GTK4/libadwaita, using MPRIS, WirePlumber, LED-class devices and evdev instead of Windows APIs. Geometry, animation timings, positioning and settings defaults reproduce the upstream values; Next-Up, the taskbar widget, acrylic blur and the global key hook are documented as non-portable rather than faked.
